xep.header:
MUC is ready This specification provides a way for MUC components to inform clients that a room is ready to be re-joined. &LEGALNOTICE; xxxx ProtoXEP Standards Track Standards Council
XMPP Core XEP-0045 XEP-0249
NOT_YET_ASSIGNED muc
Nicolas Cedilnik nicoco@nicoco.fr nicoco@nicoco.fr
0.0.1 2026-09-29 nc
First draft.

section1.p: When the service hosting a &xep0045; room shuts down, e.g., for a software upgrade, it informs XMPP clients by sending them an "unavailable" presence with a dedicated status code (332). It is then up to the client to attempt to re-join the room, either periodically, or via a user-triggered action.

This specification describes a mechanism for the MUC service to inform XMPP clients that the MUC service is now operational again, and that rooms are ready to be re-joined. This removes the need for periodic re-tries, reducing client-generated traffic. It also prevents situations where a user expects to still "be in a room" and receive its live messages when their client actually expects a manual action from them.

ul.li: MUC service restarts independently of the XMPP server it is a component of. Examples: independent MUC implementation, gateways.
XMPP server restarts and want to inform remote affiliated JIDs that rooms are available again and that they can join.

section1.p: When a MUC service wants to inform that it is back online, it sends XMPP clients a &xep0249; with a dedicated "ready" element in the message stanza.

example.caption: An invitation payload sent by a room after the MUC service has started

section1.example: <message from='rooms.example.org' to='user@example2.org'> <x xmlns='jabber:x:conference' jid='room@rooms.example.org' reason='The MUC service is back up and you are a member of this room. Please join!'/> <ready xmlns='urn:xmpp:muc-ready:0' /> </message>
section1.p: Supporting clients should attempt re-joining the MUC at this stage. Non-supporting XMPP clients treat this like any other invitation, so this automatically acts a fallback for them.

MUC services supporting this feature SHOULD advertise 'urn:xmpp:muc-ready:0' in the disco#features of their rooms. Clients can tweak or disable their periodic rejoin attempt behaviour based on this feature's availability for a given room or MUC service.
Clients supporting this feature SHOULD NOT display such invitations in their user interface.
This specification is not intended to replace &xep0410;; it solves a different practical issue encountered in deployments of &xep0045;.

The protocol described in this document is not necessary for local users of MUC services tightly coupled to their "host" XMPP server. Under such circumstances, the issue addressed by this specification can be tackled in a custom and possibly more efficient way, eg, by persisting occupants across restarts and not informing clients at all.

This specification could be abused to trap clients into joining rooms that the user does not intend to be an occupant of. After receiving a ready payload, clients MUST ensure that being an occupant of the room is compatible the user's intent, i.e., that the user had previously intended to join this room and did not explicitly left it since.
This specification defines a new namespace: 'urn:xmpp:muc-ready'

section1.code: <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?> <xs:schema xmlns:xs='http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema' targetNamespace='urn:xmpp:muc-ready:0' xmlns='urn:xmpp:muc-ready:0' elementFormDefault='qualified'> <xs:annotation> <xs:documentation> This schema defines the 'ready' element used to signal that a MUC service is operational and rooms are ready to be rejoined. </xs:documentation> </xs:annotation> <xs:element name='ready' /> </xs:schema>
